title: Investigation of ground-water contamination at Solid Waste Management Unit 12, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina
citation: Vroblesky, D.A., Casey, C.C., Petkewich, M.D., Lowery, M.A., Conlon, K.J., and Harrelson, L.G., 2007, Investigation of ground-water contamination at Solid Waste Management Unit 12, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2006-5311, map scale 1:1,020.
notes:
Report on chlorinated VOC ground-water contamination at SWMU12; no named stratigraphic units. Recorded hydrogeologic framework, lithology from boring logs described in text (p. 18), slug-test hydraulic conductivity (table 3, USGS 2005 column only; the Tetra Tech 2001, reanalysis and USGS 2003 columns on the left half were not recorded because column assignment is uncertain), and selected gradients and flow rates. Not recorded: VOC concentrations in soil (table 6) and ground water, water-table elevations on map figures (labels not reliably paired), age-dating table 4. Text on p. 18 gives 12MW-06S K as '0.9 to 0.21 ft/d' whereas table 3 gives 0.09 to 0.21.
Pages 34-53: plume figures (garbled), PRB and contaminant-trend discussion, summary, references, Appendix 1 well-construction data (p. 48; recorded well name, installation date, State Plane northing/easting and ground elevation; ground elevation column assigned by position because the header is garbled; screen depths not recorded) and Appendix 2 monthly water levels (pp. 49-53, about 3,000 readings; not recorded). References: recorded SC site reports and the hydrogeology methods cited; skipped general chemistry/isotope/phytoremediation literature (Barcelona, Bouwer 1989, Cordy, Dempster, Doucette, Harrington, Hunkeler, Ma, Nilsen, Poulson, Sevee, Shanklin, Sherwood Lollar, Slater, Song, Vieth, Vogel, Burken). Well 12MW-04S row shows ground elevation above riser (-0.30 ft stand-pipe).
Pages 54-66 hold only Appendix 3 (concentrations of organic compounds in ground water and surface water, 2000-2006). Not recorded: contaminant concentrations are outside the extraction scope, consistent with earlier packets. No geologic values on these pages.
Pages 67-80: end of Appendix 3 and Appendix 4 (inorganic ground-water chemistry); not recorded (outside scope). Pages 81-82: start of Appendix 5 direct-push soil boring logs (May 1, 2006). Boring 12PRBDP (p. 81) has an empty log; not recorded. Boring 12PRBDP21 recorded; the 5.5-16 ft interval is the zero-valent iron of the permeable reactive barrier, not native soil. Logs continue in the next packet. Elevation blank and water levels 'Not Measured' on the logs.
Pages 83-90: Appendix 5 direct-push soil boring logs (continued from the previous packet), all dated 5/1/2006, location only 'North Charleston, SC', elevation blank, water levels 'Not Measured'. Intervals marked 'Zero-Valent Iron' are the reactive-barrier fill, not native sediment. Boring 12PRBDP22: the second interval is printed '16-Aug' (apparently a spreadsheet date conversion of a depth range); its depths are not recorded. 12PRBDP26 log has no termination depth line. Page 91: Appendix 6A/6B VOC concentrations in temporary wells; not recorded (outside scope). Pages 93-94: back matter. Page 95: Plate 1 hydrogeologic cross sections; text layer is scrambled (labels not reliably paired with wells or depths), so not recorded.
